process_steps.input_state: elemental Al, Cu and Ti powder blend

evidence.quote: Appropriate amounts of elemental Al, Cu and TiO powder, each constituent of at least 99.5 wt% purity with a particle size of about 50–100 µm, were subjected to mechanical alloying in a high-energy planetary ball mill with 10:1 ball to powder mass ratio in a tungsten carbide (WC) coated container

process_steps.input_state: amorphous Al65Cu20Ti15 powder mixed with nano-TiO2
process_steps.output_state: 10 wt.% nano-TiO2 dispersed amorphous Al65Cu20Ti15 composite powder

evidence.quote: a mixture of amorphous Al65Cu20Ti15 and nanosized TiO2 powder of average particle size ~30 nm was subjected to an additional period of 182 h of planetary ball milling under identical milling conditions to produce a10 wt% nano-TiO2 dispersed amorphous Al65Cu20Ti15 matrix composite powder

although ductility was very low (< 1%)
typically detected at a stress of 1350-1360 MPa
the composites sintered at 400 oC under a uniaxial pressure of 8 GPa show the highest density (3.58 Mg/m3)
the presence of nano-ceramic particles in a micro/nanocrystalline aggregate is likely to induce dispersion strengthening

The precipitation of the fine and homogeneously distributed nanocrystalline oxide and inter-metallic phases in addition to the dispersion of nano-TiO2 can account for the significant increase in hardness and strength after high pressure sintering

the presence of nano-ceramic particles in a micro/nanocrystalline aggregate is likely to induce dispersion strengthening, to prevent grain coarsening and to enhance the creep strength at elevated temperatures
